newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian multimedia corridor invites participants.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian multimedia corridor invites participants.

text.p: Malaysian and foreign companies can start applying next month to set up businesses in the country's multimedia corridor project, the national Bernama news agency reported on Tuesday.
Firms could apply for Multimedia Super Corridor (MSC) status from Malaysia's Multimedia Development Corp (MDC), Bernama quoted MDC strategy manager, Norsaidatul Akmar Mazelan, as saying.

The MSC, conceived by Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, is a proposed 15 kilometre by 40 kilometre (nine miles by 25 miles) corridor stretching south from Kuala Lumpur to a new international airport and new administrative capital called Putrajaya.
Malaysia hopes to attract a variety of vendors from software designers and electronic publishers to film production houses, Internet service providers and education firms.
Companies in the high-tech corridor are expected to be operating by 2000.

"Companies with MSC status can operate in MSC and (are) entitled to the 10 MSC bill of guarantees and have a business location approved by the MDC at Cyberjaya," Norsaidatul told Bernama in an interview.
The city of Cyberjaya, where MSC companies will be located, will have 1.6 million square metres (17.22 million sq feet) of office space. It will also have 30,000 housing units.
The "bill of guarantees" include world-class physical and information infrastructure, freedom of ownership, competitive financial incentives and intellectual property protection.

Four companies have already been given MSC status -- Malaysia's Internet services provider Mimos Bhd, Telekom Malaysia Bhd, U.S.-based Sun Microsystems Inc and Japan's Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp.
Norsaidatul said Mimos, Telekom and Sun Microsystems were given MSC status before the status guidelines were prepared because they were responsible for the development of the MSC.
Mahathir held a week-long roadshow in California last month to try to persuade top information technology firms to invest in the MSC.
